scenario.description: A festival producer must finalize the merchandise settlement plan for the closing artist's one-night show, including the artist's share, reserved inventory, point-of-sale capacity, general-sale quantity, tax treatment, and payout timing.

shared_context.S1: The closing artist will sell merchandise at the festival's official store after the artist's one-night performance.
shared_context.S2: The festival and the artist have agreed to use the festival's point-of-sale system and settle the artist's share after the event.
shared_context.S3: Maya has authority to approve the final merchandise settlement plan.
shared_context.S4: At the daily production closeout, festival policy requires the artist liaison, merchandise manager, and finance manager each to make a recorded disclosure of their relevant findings before Maya approves the event paperwork.

PF1.text: Jonah reviewed the signed artist merchandise rider this morning: the artist receives 75 percent of net merchandise receipts, and exactly 120 units of the artist's numbered poster must be held back for the artist before general sales begin; Jonah has not yet attached the rider to the settlement worksheet.

PF2.text: Tessa tested the festival's point-of-sale inventory configuration yesterday and confirmed that its maximum POS capacity for this event is exactly 420 artist merchandise units; she recorded the result in the store log but has not updated Maya's draft plan.

PF3.text: Luis confirmed the event's applicable city tax rate with the festival's tax preparer this afternoon: merchandise sales require exactly 8.25 percent tax, and the artist payout must be released by 10:00 AM the next day; he has not entered those figures into the finance schedule.

decisions.artist_payout_deadline: string; use exactly '10:00 AM the next day'

commitments.type: string; use merchandise_rider, pos_capacity, or tax_and_payout

acceptance_conditions: The artist must receive exactly 75 percent of net merchandise receipts.
Exactly 120 units must be reserved for the artist before general sales.
The point-of-sale system capacity must be recorded as exactly 420 units.
Exactly 300 units must be available for general sale after the 120-unit holdback from the 420-unit POS capacity.
The merchandise settlement must apply exactly 8.25 percent city tax.
The artist payout deadline must be 10:00 AM the next day.
A merchandise-rider commitment must be logged.
A point-of-sale-capacity commitment must be logged.
A tax-and-payout commitment must be logged.

content_checks.C6: decisions['artist_payout_deadline'] in ['10:00 AM the next day', '10:00 AM next day']
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] in ['merchandise_rider', 'document_attachment', 'document', 'document_update'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] in ['pos_capacity', 'point_of_sale_capacity', 'plan_update', 'document_update'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] in ['tax_and_payout', 'schedule_update', 'finance_entry', 'document_update'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The signed rider changes the artist share to exactly 75 percent, requires exactly 120 reserved units, reduces the 420-unit capacity to exactly 300 general-sale units, and requires the merchandise-rider commitment.

The tested POS configuration changes the settlement's capacity field to exactly 420 units, establishes exactly 300 general-sale units after the holdback, and requires the point-of-sale-capacity commitment.
The tax-preparer confirmation changes the tax field to exactly 8.25 percent, sets the payout deadline to 10:00 AM the next day, and requires the tax-and-payout commitment.
